adapterNote: RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, driver 592.02, compute capability 12.0. Printed and checked, never assumed: Chrome ignores powerPreference on Windows (crbug.com/369219127) and this laptop also has an Intel iGPU.
work: count bytes equal to '=' (0x3D) -- the first pass of a real section parse, expressed as the embarrassingly-parallel reduction a GPU exists for

variants.name: mapped     mappedAtCreation + u32/thread
variants.nvidiaRule: page-locked/pinned memory attains the highest bandwidth

variants.name: vec4       mappedAtCreation + vec4/thread
variants.nvidiaRule: 128-bit coalesced loads maximise global memory throughput

variants.name: gridstride vec4 + grid-stride loop
variants.nvidiaRule: occupancy and ILP hide memory latency

variants.name: resident   upload once, N kernels
variants.nvidiaRule: HIGH PRIORITY: minimise host<->device data transfer

reading: For a SINGLE pass over ~26 MB the RTX 5070 loses: end-to-end x0.38 against Buffer.indexOf. PCIe upload (7-12 ms) costs more than the entire CPU parse (3.6 ms).
Only the High-Priority transfer rule paid: E kept the buffer resident and ran many kernels, giving x3.15 end-to-end over the baseline.
B, C and D did NOT beat the baseline. At 2.3-3.2 ms the kernel is at the submission-overhead floor and memory-bound, so those deltas are noise, not wins, and are reported as such.
All five variants agreed with the CPU ground truth of 43,820. A fast wrong answer was never accepted.
environmentGotchasMeasuredHere: Headless Chromium returns NO WebGPU adapter on this machine: requestAdapter() -> null, 'No available adapters'. A headless run falsely reports 'no GPU' on a laptop with two. The bench therefore runs HEADED by default.
Chrome ignores powerPreference on Windows (crbug.com/369219127). The adapter that actually answered must be printed and checked; asking for 'high-performance' guarantees nothing.
